A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same APT research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and regression benchmarks, component ablations, convergence measurements and synthetic-generator analyses in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, ablation, convergence and synthetic-generator results, including the per-dataset appendix results.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 and new Appendix B introduce optional batchwise prediction, using size-weighted classification predictions and inverse-variance regression aggregation, plus feature-patch embedding with attention and pooling. These substantially extend the documented input and inference procedures. The original adversarial pre-training and mixture block remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same OpenML-CC18 classification and OpenML-CTR23 regression suites, their small-dataset subsets, and synthetic-generator scenarios. The new scalability appendix reports no additional dataset or task evaluation.

E2.justification: Tables 1–5 retain identical comparator memberships, including the GBDT, TabPFN, conventional machine-learning and neural baselines, and the same component variants. Newly cited scaling methods are not benchmarked.

E3.justification: The reported experiments retain their 80/20 splits, metrics, one-hour comparison budget, 100-feature subsampling and pre-training settings. Appendix B describes optional scaling procedures without identifying a new experiment or a revision to the existing evaluations.

E4.justification: The generator-distribution analysis, categorical-feature and missing-value breakdowns, class-count generalization tests, convergence curves and component ablations are retained. No additional robustness or sensitivity analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions already report standard deviations across five splits and explain both AUC standard-deviation aggregation conventions. Appendix B's uncertainty-weighted prediction is an inference procedure, not additional experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the empirical plots are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains APT's 0.921 mean ROC-AUC and 0.90-second mean runtime; Table 4 retains all-dataset MSEs of 0.306 for APT and 0.340 for TabPFN.

T1.justification: Appendix A revises the Bayesian factorization by removing test-input conditioning and likelihood terms, and adds a derivation connecting expected KL divergence to the existing negative-log-likelihood objective. Appendix B adds predictive-aggregation formulas. These are bounded mathematical additions rather than a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same scientific contributions: adversarial pre-training, removal of the class-count restriction, faster convergence and strong tabular prediction performance. The revised conclusion preserves these claims; optional scalability adaptations are not promoted as a new central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 newly cautions that inherited TabPFN priors and hyperparameters may favor classification over regression. The conclusion replaces output-cardinality speculation with possible mixture-block extensions and inductive-bias arguments, while retaining the large-dataset performance and complexity limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies a 3,000-sample inference batch cap, weighting rules, patch-padding instructions and optional positional encodings. Existing training hyperparameters remain unchanged. Conversely, v2 removes v1's explicit code URL, retaining only the supplementary-code reference.

R1.justification: v2 discusses Hollmann et al. (2025) and TabICL as compatible scaling approaches and adds references supporting patch embedding, positional encoding and longer contexts. It removes the TuneTables discussion and reference. The broader PFN and adversarial-learning positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction and conclusion rewrites, terminology refinements from MLP to dense layers, expanded appendix explanations and a new impact statement. Adding Appendix B renumbers the existing hyperparameter and results appendices without substantially reorganizing the main narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adjusts the illustrative generator icons, and Figure 2 redraws the mixture block with explicit feedforward, dot-product, softmax and Concrete branches. Existing tables and empirical plots are preserved, with changes to placement and surrounding layout.

improvement.justification: The clearer mixture-block diagram, fuller explanation of the training objective, regression qualification and concrete scaling instructions modestly improve clarity and usefulness. The scaling additions have no accompanying validation, and removing the explicit code URL weakens accessibility. Overall, the explanatory gains outweigh that limited loss, while the empirical support remains unchanged.
